# 1 Enoch Chapter 9 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of the Watchers

---

**1** Then Michael, Uriel, Raphael, and Gabriel looked down from heaven and saw the abundance of blood that was being shed upon the earth, and all the lawlessness that was being committed upon it.

**2** And they said to one another: 'The desolated earth cries out, and the sound of their crying ascends to the gates of heaven.'

**3** 'And now, to you, O holy ones of heaven, the souls of men make their plea, saying: Bring our cause before the Most High.'

**4** And they said to the Lord of the ages: 'Lord of lords, God of gods, King of kings, God of the ages — the throne of Your glory stands through all the generations of the ages, and Your name is holy and glorious and blessed through all the ages.

**5** You have made all things, and authority over all things is Yours. All things are naked and open before Your sight, and You see all things, and nothing can hide from You.

**6** You have seen what Azazel has done — how he has taught all unrighteousness on the earth and revealed the eternal secrets that were preserved in heaven, which men were striving to learn.

**7** And Shemihazah, to whom You gave authority to rule over his companions —

**8** they have gone to the daughters of men on the earth, and have lain with the women, and have defiled themselves, and have revealed to them every manner of sin.

**9** And the women have borne giants, and the whole earth has been filled with blood and unrighteousness.

**10** And now, behold, the souls of those who have died cry out and make their plea at the gates of heaven, and their groaning has ascended and cannot cease because of the lawless deeds committed on the earth.

**11** And You know all things before they come to pass, and You see these things and You permit them, and You do not tell us what we should do regarding them.'


---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering from the Ge'ez text, preserving sentence structure and key theological vocabulary while producing readable English prose. Paragraph divisions follow the sense units of the Ge'ez.*
